methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $117M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
VEIR, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Tim Heidel, has raised $117M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (LNZA) operating in the same sector, including stage-adjacent players such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods are applicable here. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $117M total raised as a proxy for post-money value, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $222M. Peer-median valuation across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) produces a $1.0B median, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. 

Triangulating these two methods produces a low estimate of $189M, a median of $611M, and a high of $1.1B. The spread reflects meaningful uncertainty in peer selection and stage comparability; KoBold Metals' $3.0B valuation as a Series C creates material upside, while stage-progression methodology assumes disciplined step-ups. The peer-median approach carries elevated weight given direct sector and stage alignment, though early-stage climate-tech valuations remain volatile and contingent on technology de-risking and commercialization progress.
